Introduction
What is Big Data?
● Big data is data that exceeds the processing capacity of conventional 
database systems.
● The data is too big, moves too fast, or doesn’t fit the structures of your 
database architectures.
● To gain value from this data, you must choose an alternative way to 
process it.

Characteristics of Big Data
● Big Data is characterized by the 5 V’s.

slides.text:
Characteristics of Big Data
● Volume – massive amounts of data
● Velocity – speed of data generation & processing
● Variety – structured, semi-structured, unstructured data
● Veracity – data quality, accuracy, trustworthiness
● Value – extracting meaningful insights

Characteristics of Big Data
Volume
● Definition: Scale of data (TBs, PBs, ZBs)
● Example: Facebook generates ~4PB/day
● The main challenges of managing huge data include storage limitations, 
processing power requirements, and bandwidth capabilities.

● Real-time analytics allows companies to respond instantly to changing

Variety
● Definition: Structured, semi-structured, unstructured
● Examples: Tables, JSON/XML, images, videos, tweets
● Challenges: Too many data sources and the data is not properly organized 
and managed.

Veracity
● Veracity: Accuracy, trustworthiness

Characteristics of Big Data
Value
● Value: Extracting insights for decision-making.
● It is not just the amount of data that we store or process. 
● It is actually the amount of valuable, reliable and trustworthy data that 
needs to be stored, processed, analyzed to find insights.

Types of Big Data
Structured Data
● highly organized and resides in fixed fields.
● straightforward to store, retrieve, and analyze.
● fits neatly into relational databases or spreadsheets.
● ideal for traditional data analysis techniques.
● is easy to manage but often represents only a fraction of the total data 
available.

Semi structured Data
● combines elements of both structured and unstructured data. 
● It has an organizational framework, such as tags or markers. 
● but lacks the rigid format of relational databases.
● bridges the gap between the flexibility of unstructured data and the 
organization of structured data.

Types of Big Data
Semi structured Data
Examples:

● E-commerce Product Catalogs: Products are described using structured
attributes (like price and stock) alongside unstructured descriptions.
Applications:

Sources of Big Data
● Social media platforms (Facebook, Twitter, Instagram)
● IoT devices & sensors (smart homes, wearables)
● Business transactions (e-commerce, banking)
● Healthcare systems (patient records, medical imaging)
● Scientific research (genomics, astronomy)
● Government & public data (census, traffic monitoring)

Introduction to Big Data Analytics
What is Data Analytics?
● Data analytics is a discipline focused on extracting insights from data.
● It comprises the processes, tools and techniques of data analysis and 
management, including the collection, organization, and storage of data.
● The chief aim of data analytics is to apply statistical analysis and 
technologies on data to find trends and solve problems.

Introduction to Big Data Analytics
What is Data Analytics?
● Data analytics has become increasingly important in the enterprise as a 
means for analyzing and shaping business processes and improving 
decision-making and business results.
● Data analytics draws from a range of disciplines — including computer 
programming, mathematics, and statistics — to perform analysis on data 
in an effort to describe, predict, and improve performance.
● To ensure robust analysis, data analytics teams leverage a range of data 
management techniques, including data mining, data cleansing, data 
transformation, data modeling, and more.

Introduction to Big Data Analytics
What is Big Data Analytics?
● Big data analytics refers to collecting, processing, cleaning, and analyzing 
large datasets to help organizations operationalize their big data.
● Big data analytics describes the process of uncovering trends, patterns, 
and correlations in large amounts of raw data to help make 
data-informed decisions.
● Big data analytics is the use of advanced analytic techniques against very 
large, diverse data sets that include structured, semi-structured and 
unstructured data, from different sources, and in different sizes from 
terabytes to zettabytes.
